newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major calls windfall tax "politics of envy".
newsitem.headline: UK's Major calls windfall tax "politics of envy".

text.p: A windfall tax on privatised British utilities, as proposed by the opposition Labour Party, will hit consumers and shareholders, Prime Minister John Major said on Thursday.
"The windfall tax is straightforward politics of envy," Major said on Sky Television.
He said Labour's finance spokesman Gordon Brown was seeking to fund a whole series of expenditure pledges. "He thinks he has found a cheap and popular way of raising the money."

But consumers' electricity bills would rise and shareholders would suffer, he said. "Gordon Brown might like to pretend to people he is hitting the fat cats at the top of the industry, he is not. He's hitting the consumer and he is hitting the shareholders of which there are millions."

Brown said on Thursday he would levy a one-off windfall tax on Britain's utilities shortly after the election and spend three billion pounds ($4.9 billion) of the proceeds to help young people and the long-term unemployed find work.
